blocks.x: Detection engineering with measured coverage: threat-informed detection mapped to the techniques that actually target your sector, purple-teamed quarterly, and run by a SOC whose speed is measured from first signal to containment — not from alert to acknowledgement.
Detection coverage is a measurement, not a maturity score

A SOC earns trust with two numbers: how fast it contains what matters, and how much of the attacker playbook it can actually see. We run detection engineering against threat-informed attack paths, validate coverage with purple-team drills, and measure everything from first signal to containment.

Managed SOC here means an operating rhythm, not a headcount: triage SLAs, escalation ladders, threat-intel feeds that turn into detections within days, and the post-incident loop that turns every incident into new coverage.
Below: the failure modes that flood SOCs and hide real threats, the reference architecture of measured detection, and the console that reports speed honestly.
Four ways SOC programs drown in their own alerts
Each failure mode exhausts the analysts while the real attack walks past — the countermeasures buy back precision and make coverage falsifiable.

widgets.title: SOC response fabric — click nodes for the playbook contract

nodes.label: Estate telemetry
nodes.detail: Endpoints, identity, network and cloud logs normalized to one schema — detection quality is bounded by telemetry quality upstream.

nodes.label: Intel pipeline
nodes.detail: Sector feeds, ISAC traffic and finished profiles screened for applicability; indicators promoted with context or not at all.

nodes.label: Detection-as-code
nodes.detail: Versioned rules with replay-tested precision scores, ATT&CK mapping and CI deployment — detections are software.

nodes.label: Tier-1 auto-triage
nodes.detail: Enrichment, dedup and playbook-driven dispositions for the repetitive classes — analysts see the survivors with context attached.

nodes.label: Tier-2 investigation
nodes.detail: Human investigation with the evidence graph pre-built; escalations carry a written narrative, not a raw alert.

nodes.label: Threat hunting
nodes.detail: Hypothesis-driven hunts against the coverage gaps — every hunt ends in a rule, a telemetry request, or a documented negative.

nodes.label: Response playbooks
nodes.detail: Containment actions pre-authorized per severity with reversibility-first ordering; execution measured in the game days.

widgets.note: Click nodes for the contract each layer carries. Hunting feeds the rule repo — the SOC learns from what it looks for, not only from what fires.
